html:
The Gun War was fought from 1880 to 1881 in Basutoland between the Basotho and the Cape Colony, which had ordered them to hand in their guns.

Many Basotho men had bought rifles with wages from the diamond fields at Kimberley. When the Cape government, then ruling Basutoland, demanded the guns, most chiefs refused and fought. Cape forces could not defeat them in the mountains.

The peace let the Basotho keep their guns for a licence fee. The war's cost led the Cape to give up the territory, and in 1884 Britain took it back under direct rule, which in the end kept Lesotho from becoming part of South Africa. It was one of the few colonial wars in the region the Africans did not lose, decades after the Free State wars.
sum: The Gun War was fought from 1880 to 1881 in Basutoland between the Basotho and the Cape Colony, which had ordered them to hand in their guns.
